newsitem.title: USA: Florida fires employee over leaked AIDS list.
newsitem.headline: Florida fires employee over leaked AIDS list.

text.p: A Florida health worker has been fired for allegedly using confidential state data on AIDS and HIV patients to screen his dates and look up names for friends, authorities said on Thursday.

William Calvert III, a health investigator with the state Department of Health and Rehabilitative Services, was fired on Wednesday for what state officials called a critical breach of the public trust.

Calvert, whose job it was to collect names as part of a national network tracking AIDS cases, had been on paid administrative leave for three weeks after allegations arose that he used a list of AIDS and HIV-infected residents to look up names of potential dates for himself and his friends.

The list, which included the names of nearly 4,000 people with AIDS and HIV in the Tampa Bay area, is thought to be the same one sent on computer discs last month to the St. Petersburg Times and Tampa Tribune, the Times reported.

An anonymous letter sent with the discs accused Calvert of circulating the list in a bar and offering to look up names for friends. Officials have called the case the nation's largest security breach of AIDS information.
"Mr. Calvert admitted that he used the information," said HRS spokesman Terry Welch. "And if that is the truth, then that is why Mr. Calvert no longer works for the agency.
"The public pays him to protect their information and they pay us to do the same thing," said Welch. "He has to meet that standard."
Calvert has claimed that he is being used as a scapegoat to cover up lax security within the HRS system, which is part of a nationwide network to gather data on AIDS and HIV-infected people.

Calvert also contends that a former business partner leaked a disc copy of the file and an anonymous letter to the two newspapers in Tampa implicating him. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement was conducting its own investigation into the leak.
Calvert's attorney, Lee Fugate of Tampa, could not immediately be reached for comment on Thursday. Calvert has until 5 p.m. EDt Friday to respond to the HRS charges.
